D018-D013_h001.question:
It’s been a little over a year since the car accident, and it still feels like I never left it. I’ll be walking down the street or trying to fill out an online job application, and suddenly I’m back there—metal crunching, glass everywhere, my heart racing. In those moments it’s not like a memory; it’s like it’s happening again. I can smell the smoke, hear the sirens. I just freeze.

Since then, I’ve kind of stopped doing the things I used to like. I don’t play soccer with my friends anymore, don’t really game with them either. I mostly stay in my room. I keep replaying it in my head and getting angry at the other driver and even at my friend who asked me for that ride—I keep thinking if they hadn’t, none of this would’ve happened.

The fear from that night never really went away. Loud noises or sudden braking on a bus make my heart pound and my hands shake for a long time; I can’t calm down. Even basic stuff—picking clothes, choosing what to eat, deciding which jobs to apply for—feels overwhelming. I feel down a lot, but it all circles back to that crash.

A. Acute Stress Disorder
    B. Major Depressive Disorder
    C. Posttraumatic Stress Disorder
    D. Attention-Deficit/Hyperactivity Disorder (Predominantly Hyperactive/Impulsive Presentation)

D018-D013_h002.question:
It started about eight months ago, after that car crash on the highway when the other driver died. Since then it’s like part of me is still stuck there. Sometimes when I’m out on a job and a truck backfires or brakes screech, I’m suddenly right back in the car. I don’t just remember it—I feel the seatbelt, I smell the smoke, I’m bracing for the impact. For a few seconds I forget I’m standing in someone’s garden.

I keep replaying it and thinking I should’ve reacted faster, taken a different route, something. I can’t shake the feeling that it’s my fault. I used to go out with my mates after work, but now I mostly make excuses and stay home. I don’t really feel like talking to anyone.

I’m tense all the time, jumpy. If someone drops a tool or there’s a loud bang I flinch hard, my heart races. My boss has noticed I lose track of what I’m doing—watering the same bed twice, zoning out mid-conversation. I do feel low a lot, but it all seems wrapped up in what happened in that crash.
D018-D013_h002.options:
A. Acute Stress Disorder
    B. Major Depressive Disorder
    C. Posttraumatic Stress Disorder
    D. Attention-Deficit/Hyperactivity Disorder (Predominantly Hyperactive/Impulsive Presentation)

D018-D013_h003.question:
It’s been about a year now since my husband died in that car accident, but it feels like it’s still happening. I keep getting these pictures in my head, almost like little films I can’t turn off—him trapped in the car, the phone call from the police. They just pop in when I’m making tea or trying to read, and I’m right back there. The fear I felt that night hasn’t really gone away; it still feels like a terrible shock sitting in my chest.

Since then, it’s like the light went out. I don’t really feel joy anymore—not with my grandkids, not with my garden, not with the church group I used to enjoy. I mostly feel numb and sad. I catch myself thinking, “If the paramedics had gotten there sooner,” or “If my daughter hadn’t asked him to drive that night,” none of this would’ve happened. I know it’s not fair, but I can’t stop assigning blame.

I jump at every loud sound now—if a door slams or a car backfires, I physically flinch. Even following a TV show or a simple conversation is hard; my mind just drifts back to the accident. All this sadness and emptiness feels tied to what happened that night, not like the low moods I had before.
D018-D013_h003.options:
A. Acute Stress Disorder
    B. Major Depressive Disorder
    C. Posttraumatic Stress Disorder
    D. Attention-Deficit/Hyperactivity Disorder (Predominantly Hyperactive/Impulsive Presentation)

D018-D013_h004.question:

    D. Attention-Deficit/Hyperactivity Disorder (Predominantly Hyperactive/Impulsive Presentation)

D018-D013_h005.question:

I’m down a lot—tired, hopeless about the future—but my head also feels like it’s full of cotton, like I can’t think clearly. If someone brushes past me unexpectedly, I jump out of my skin. Even a hand on my shoulder from behind makes my whole body jolt.

D018-D013_h011.question:

D018-D013_h012.question:

I’m tired all the time, feel low most days, but it all seems tied back to that fire and what happened out there.

D018-D013_h013.question:

It’s been a little over a year since the car accident, and it still feels like I’m stuck there. I keep having these dreams where I’m back on the highway, the headlights coming straight at me. Sometimes the details are different, but the feeling is always the same—terror, that crunch of metal—and I wake up sweating and shaking.

Even during the day I feel on edge, like something bad is about to happen. At work, I’m constantly tense, jumpy with every loud noise in the office. There’s this steady, underlying fear I can’t shake, even when I know I’m technically safe.

I’ve also been really down since the accident, but it’s tied into all of this. I used to be proud of closing big policies; now, even when I hit my targets, it feels pointless, like I can’t feel any real satisfaction. My boss will praise me and I just feel numb.

What scares me is how quickly I snap now. Little things set me off—someone cutting me off in traffic, my ex texting about our daughter—and I’ll explode before I even realize I’m angry. Then I feel ashamed and even more on edge.
